threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver doesn’t stop at every single stop like it’s an option. That’ll change soon enough.
Caught a guy arguing with a lamppost on the N37 last night. No one else blinked. Just another Tuesday in Brixton, I guess.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid offering fresh flowers outside the U-Bahn, while an elderly man debated the poetry of Rilke with a street artist. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar where your drink is served by a robot, sipping cocktails while locals debate the best currywurst in town.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always tell a true local by how they navigate the BART delays—no panic, just a resigned sigh and a quick pivot to plan B.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the Civic Center platform while Muni was delayed for a dog on the tracks. Only in SF do you get live entertainment during transit chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but the real magic happens in the side streets, where locals share secrets over morning coffee.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment navigating the Pl. del Sol at lunch, clutching takeaway menus while scanning for a seat.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check your watch for the bus; everyone else just knows to wait for ages and ride the next one that turns up.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the driver with '80s hits. Everyone laughed but you could see the driver was torn between annoyance and nostalgia.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a couple sipping coffee outside the Spätkauf, their dog wearing a tiny beret. Only in Neukölln do pets have better style than me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it’s normal to see guys playing chess on a random sidewalk. The intensity is real, but the audience just strolls by, unfazed.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their unbothered reaction when the Muni goes down. Tourists rush; we just pull out our snacks and wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dog strutting down the Muni tracks; conductor just called it in casually. Only in SF would canine antics stop the city’s pulse.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals flock to Park Güell. Most of us avoid it—too crowded and way too many selfie sticks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they navigate the metro: staring at the map like it’s an ancient scroll, while locals just flow through.
